The U.S. government has not officially confirmed the bomb’s purpose.

The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, new research has found.

In that period, 403 “hyperscalers” – the largest datacenters used primarily to handle the growth of artificial intelligence – emitted about 25.7m metric tons of carbon dioxide, according to the study.

Former US vice-president at Cop31 urges lawmakers to rethink contentious bipartisan Baaja bill advanced by the US Senate

It would be a “serious mistake” to pass a contentious bipartisan bill to speed up energy projects and datacenters that has divided Democrats and environmentalists, Al Gore said.

The legislation, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Baaja), will make it easier to build large infrastructure projects in the US, from oil and gas pipelines and datacenters to crucial clean energy components such as solar and wind power and transmission lines, scaling back environmental protections and legal challenges in order to do so.

items.summary_raw: Nuno Felix RT @PascalJouary: Des soldats français opèrent depuis plusieurs mois en Ukraine, selon les informations recueillies et corroborées par RFI. Il ne s’agit pas de combattre mais d’apporter un soutien aux forces de Kiev. Leur mission : veiller aux équipements de l’armée ukrainienne et dispenser des formations. Le nom de cette structure : Volia, avec un général français à sa tête. En ukrainien, le mot « volia » résume l’esprit de résistance, le combat pour la liberté. Volia est un dispositif hautement confidentiel, jusque-là passé sous les radars.  Afin de garantir la confidentialité de cette présence militaire française dans un pays en guerre, il a été décidé, selon plusieurs sources proches du dossier avec qui RFI s’est entretenue, de s’appuyer sur la mission Gerfaut. Cette dernière, officiellement assumée, est un détachement militaire français présent en Pologne depuis février 2023 (notamment sur le camp de Wedrzyn, au nord-ouest de la Pologne) dans le cadre de la mission européenne EUMAM-Ukraine, prorogée pour une nouvelle période de deux ans, jusqu'au 15 novembre 2028.  🔴 URGENT -  Mission «Volia»: comment l'armée française opère en Ukraine ➡️ https://go.rfi.fr/vqH https

items.title: Europe’s Wadden Sea is a natural wonder. So why might it join the world heritage in danger list?
items.summary_raw:
Along the coasts of the Netherlands, Germany and Denmark, its intertidal flats host a wealth of marine life and birds. But extraction industries, tourism and fishing are taking their toll

Stand on the coastline at high tide and you look out over unbroken water, with sandy islands rising a few miles offshore. A few hours later and the view across the Wadden Sea has transformed into a maze of deep channels, drying sandbanks, salt marshes and mud flats.

As the largest unbroken system of intertidal sand and mud flats in the world, this ever-changing habitat stretches hundreds of miles along the north European coasts of Germany, Denmark and the Netherlands and was awarded world heritage status by Unesco in 2009.

Aerial view of the unique features of the Wadden Sea coast. Photograph: Janis Meyer/CWSS

items.summary_raw:
António Guterres says climate action central to every aspect of UN’s work, as leaders depart Cop31 and talks go on

Tackling the climate crisis is central to all of human life and must be at the forefront of global governance, the outgoing UN secretary general has said in an emotional farewell address at the Cop31 climate summit.

“You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” António Guterres said at his final climate press conference as secretary general on Friday. “You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it. You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends.”

Turkey and Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s office said on Friday. 

Erdogan said Ankara and Doha would continue working together to prevent a resurgence of war in the region. His office said the agreement would “add a new dimension to relations between Turkiye and Qatar”.

Erdogan met Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul, where the two leaders co-chaired a meeting of the countries’ Supreme Strategic Committee.

items.title: A super El Niño brings startling changes for marine life on California coast: ‘like nothing we’ve ever seen’
items.summary_raw:
Water temperatures are climbing the charts, high tides are swallowing the shoreline and vital parts of the food web that feed ocean diversity are disappearing

On a picturesque autumn afternoon last week, the beaches of California’s Monterey Bay were teeming with life and death.

A cadre of shorebirds charged and retreated in a synchronized dance with the raging surf. Nearby, the receding tides had deposited lifeless bundles of feathers and bone, tangled in piles of glistening kelp. Swollen sea lion carcasses, their teeth bared in a quiet grimace, dotted the sand as beach picnickers and dog walkers enjoyed the warm, cloudless day.

Asked to comment on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s departure as President of the Republic of Cyprus Nikos Christodoulides entered the summit venue in Antalya, Papadopoulos described the move as “a diplomatic discourtesy.” “But one fact remains: the Republic of Cyprus was the only internationally recognized state on the island represented at the United Nations Climate Change Conference,” he said. The president, he added, represented the Republic of Cyprus, spoke on behalf of Cyprus at the summit, and was the one who took part in the summit’s family photo.

items.title: Trump the ‘biggest loser’ for scrapping climate action, John Kerry says at Cop31
items.summary_raw:
Kerry decries president for ceding clean-energy dominance to China and says climate crisis still a key issue for voters

Donald Trump is the “biggest loser we’ve seen in a long time” for scrapping action on the climate crisis and ceding the clean energy race to China, former US secretary of state John Kerry has said.

Kerry, speaking at the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey, criticized Trump for withdrawing the US from the international climate process and axing measures that reduced planet-heating emissions. Unlike almost all other countries in the world, the Trump administration has sent no delegation to the resort city of Antalya for the annual UN climate talks, which started on Monday.

items.summary_raw:
Proponents argue ocean carbon removal is necessary to counteract the effects of the climate crisis but critics say more research is needed

A cluster of candy cane-striped smoke stacks dots the horizon of Tufts Cove in Nova Scotia, Canada. Deep in the briny depths of Halifax harbour, something huge is happening: the ocean is being engineered to remove atmospheric carbon.

“This is what Mother Nature has done naturally for a few billion years in order to rebalance the atmospheric and ocean chemistry over long timescales,” says Dr Greg Rau, co-founder and senior scientist at Planetary Technologies.

items.summary_raw:
Since the US war on Iran began in February, there have been hundreds of oil spills, posing a ‘generational’ threat to wildlife

The vast, dark slicks in the strait of Hormuz are visible from space. Throughout October, oil tankers were struck by missiles or sea mines in the waterway and spilled crude into the sea. The pollution has spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening to cause lasting damage to marine ecosystems that are home to dolphins, sea turtles and countless species of fish.

Eight months into the war between the US and Iran, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes has become a battlefield and the centre of a growing environmental disaster.

items.title: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns
items.summary_raw:
Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says

The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.

Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year.

items.title: ‘The world we know is over’ without urgent climate action, leaders tell Cop31

Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms

Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit.

Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.

items.title: AI datacentres plan on-site power stations on huge scale despite climate risks, research reveals
items.summary_raw:
181GW of gas-fired capacity proposed for sites in US and Europe because of delays in connecting to national grids, says report

Developers of AI datacentres plan to build on-site climate-destroying gas power stations on a huge scale to meet their energy demands, research reveals.

Datacentres planned across the US, the UK and mainland Europe have proposals to build fossil fuel plants on-site to create 181GW of gas-fired capacity because of delays to connect to national grids, according to the findings. This is almost four times the total peak electricity demand of Great Britain.

This is how it works. An industry puts tremendous effort into resisting change: lobbying governments, mobilising the media, pouring money into junktanks. It argues that a transition would threaten jobs, or damage the national interest, or harm poor people, while what it really fears is the cost of retooling its plants or developing new protocols. Then, when the inevitable cliff edge approaches, it whines that change is coming too soon. For reasons beyond its control, it isn’t ready, so the government must delay its plans.

items.title: Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio Elected to Lead House Republicans in the Minority
items.summary_raw:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio won the race Tuesday to serve as House Republican leader as the party prepares for its new role in the minority and a flurry of Democratic investigations aimed at its standard-bearer in the White House. Jordan, who serves as chairman of the House Judiciary Committee, defeated Rep. Steve Scalise of Louisiana in a secret-ballot election of Republicans who will serve in the next Congress. The vote was 106-73. Jordan, 62, is a co-founder of the ultraconservative House Freedom Caucus and served as its first chairman. His candidacy appealed to those looking for new leadership in the wake of last week’s election debacle and to those who like his hard-hitting political style. “The way that Jim fights says a lot about where this conference is,” said Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla., who nominated Jordan to serve as minority leader.

The post Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio Elected to Lead House Republicans in the Minority appeared first on The National Herald.

items.title: Abeille Marengo Sails to Begin Greece-Cyprus Cable Surveys as Turkey Claims Its Consent Was Obtained, Athens Pushes Back
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS - The French research vessel Abeille Marengo sailed from the port of Heraklion at 6:26 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, to begin seabed surveys for the Greece-Cyprus electricity interconnection. Hours later, Turkey issued a new NAVTEX concerning the vessel’s activities, claiming that the surveys had been coordinated with the competent Turkish authorities and that their consent had been obtained, prompting a response from Athens. The Abeille Marengo, which had arrived in Crete from Italy and remained at the port of Heraklion pending the start of operations, departed with the assistance of a tugboat after a pilot boarded the vessel. It is initially expected to calibrate its scientific equipment before beginning seabed mapping along the planned cable route, from the Korakia area of Heraklion to Cyprus. The work includes hydrographic and geotechnical surveys, seabed sampling, penetration tests, and drilling, using specialized equipment such as multibeam echosounders, side-scan sonar, and magnetometers.

items.title: US Soldier Arrested in UK Spy Probe
items.summary_raw:
British counter-terrorism police arrested a U.S. Army member near Gloucester on suspicion of espionage linked to Russia.

The 41-year-old is in custody at a London police station. He was detained under Sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act 2023.

Two properties in Gloucestershire are being searched. MI5, the FBI and the U.S. military are working the case with UK police.

Per BBC News and LBC.

items.title: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
items.summary_raw:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.

As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
